title: Traffic anticipation pocket charts & decision tree (Feb 2028)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operator-friendly canvas that combines small pocket charts (expected QPS/latency relationships), an explicit decision tree for surge/microwindow responses, and a short release notes draft to seed customer comms. Meant for the 48h preflight and the first 6 hours post-traffic-shift.

Context and scope:
- Applies to hosted API + Dedicated mixed rollouts where traffic will be ramped in 3 microwindows (0%, 20%, 60%, 100%).
- Focus on user-visible latency and error budgets; cost signals are secondary but included for ops tuning.
- This is an ops-facing sketch; will be refined into the formal runbook once we lock the rollout timeline.

Quick pocket charts (operator cheat-sheet):
1) Expected QPS uplift vs P95 latency (approx)
   - baseline QPS: 1k sustained per shard
   - +20% traffic (microwindow 1): expect P95 + 5–12ms, CPU +8%, GPU mem unchanged
   - +60% traffic (microwindow 2): expect P95 + 18–45ms, CPU +25–40%, GPU mem +3–8%
   - +100% traffic (full): expect P95 + 25–70ms, careful of tail spikes if batching increases

2) Failure modes & quick indicators
   - model-routing-fanout: sudden increase in KV cache misses -> rising p50 token-time and increased kernel-switch logs
   - queue-steal/backpressure: RLQueue depth > 300ms lead time -> degrade responses or 429s
   - degraded-variants fallback: invocation rate of fallback pathways > 5% sustained -> inspect model health

Decision tree (condensed operator flow):
- Step 0: baseline checks (preflight, within 48h): telemetry hooks, smoke tests, canary small traffic generator running 30m.
- Step 1: after moving to microwindow 1 (20%): monitor for 15m. If p95 latency <= expected + 25ms AND error rate < 0.5% then proceed to microwindow 2.
  - If p95 > expected + 25ms OR error rate >= 0.5%: pause. Run the quick mitigation list: reduce batch size override by 10%, clear prefix cache (if safe), and route 5% of traffic to fallback-variant. If no improvement in 10m -> rollback to baseline and open an incident.
- Step 2: at microwindow 2 (60%): monitor for 30m. Tolerances: p95 <= expected + 40ms, error rate < 1.0%.
  - If error rate climbs between 1.0–2.0%: enable adaptive-throttle at 50% of added traffic and notify SRE for manual tune.
  - If error rate > 2.0% OR p95 > expected + 60ms: initiate controlled unwind to 20% and run regression checklist.
- Step 3: full traffic: watch the following for first 2 hours: sustained CPU/GPU > 85%, RLQueue depth > 250ms, fallback-rate > 5%. Any of these -> initiate partial backoff lane (reduce to 60%) and open postmortem timeline.

Telemetry signal definitions (exact metric names for dashboards):
- api.p95_gen_latency_ms (global)
- api.error_rate_1m (client-side errors aggregated)
- runtime.kernel-switch-count (per-host)
- batch.avg_size (per-model)
- routing.fallback_pct (per-customer)
- infra.gpu_util_pct (per-pool)

Threshold table (for quick paste into alerts):
- WARNING: api.p95_gen_latency_ms > baseline_p95 + 25ms for 5m OR api.error_rate_1m >= 0.5% -> severity: P3 notify on-call and release channel
- CRITICAL: api.p95_gen_latency_ms > baseline_p95 + 60ms for 3m OR api.error_rate_1m >= 2% for 3m -> severity: P1 page SRE and kickoff rollback
- INFRA: infra.gpu_util_pct > 90% for 10m -> scale-suggestion to infra team and consider routing policy fallback

Runbook quick mitigations (ordered, quick to execute):
1) Throttle: apply adaptive-throttle for non-critical routes (route policy ID: rp-adaptive-01)
2) Batch-size override: set batch.max_tokens to conservative profile (batch-ops/override-2028-02)
3) Drain/replace: cordon a host if kernel-switch-count is anomalous and replace from warm pool
4) Fallback rotation: flip 5–10% traffic to compatible quantized model variant (variant id: q8-v2)
5) Rollback: announce rollback on #release-ops, execute traffic shift to previous stable config, and set status to "rollback in progress" in release tracker.

Rollout calendar (compact):
- T-48h: finalize canary traffic generator and run 4 smoke loops (owner: Linh)
- T-24h: run full telemetry rehearsal (owner: Diego)
- T-2h: dry-run ramp script with toggles (owner: Maya)
- T+0: launch microwindow 1 (20%) -> monitor 15m
- T+30m: escalate to microwindow 2 (60%) -> monitor 30m
- T+90m: full traffic -> monitor 2h

Preflight checklist (tickboxes):
- [ ] Smoke tests green (end-to-end with auth, billing paths)
- [ ] Release artifacts uploaded and signed in artifact-registry
- [ ] Capacity reservations verified with infra for GPU pools
- [ ] Observability: dashboards shared and alert rules staged
- [ ] On-call roster confirmed for first 6 hours post-shift
- [ ] Communications templates loaded in Slack draft channel

Draft release notes (customer-facing seed):
Headline: "Lower-latency serving and more predictable throughput for production inference"
Short blurb: "This release improves serving efficiency and expands the model routing heuristics that reduce cold-prefix latency for common workloads. You may see slightly higher throughput limits for bursty workloads and improved fallbacks when a pool is constrained."
Notable changes:
- Improved prefix KV caching heuristics (reduces cold-start latency for multi-turn chat)
- Model routing improvements for cheaper-compatible variants (reduces requeues)
- New admin config to override batching per-route
Potential impact:
- Brief increases in P95 latency are possible during staged rollouts; we gate by 2% error-rate thresholds and will roll back if necessary.

Operator notes / ideas to follow up:
- Build a tiny canary that injects artificial KV-miss patterns to test routing resilience (ticket: JIRA-1302).
- Automate rollback annotation in release tracker with the active metric anchors (low-effort, big help for postmortems).
- Consider a soft-surge lane that increases batch frequency rather than batch size for high-QPS non-chat endpoints.

Slack template (post to #release-ops at rollout steps):
"@here Starting rollout: microwindow 1 (20%) for release X. Watch api.p95_gen_latency_ms and api.error_rate_1m. Alerts: P3 if p95 > +25ms or error >= 0.5%. On-call: @linh @diego @maya. If we hit critical thresholds, follow decision tree in the doc. Update thread with 'GO->60%' or 'PAUSE->rollback'"

Known issues (preflight):
- Some GPU hosts show intermittent kernel-switch spikes under synthetic batch shapes (logs: infra-kernel-2028-01). Plan: cordon noisy hosts before full traffic.
- Small percentage of routes still use legacy routing table and will not pick up batch-size override; we have a migration PR in progress (github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/392).

Next steps (short):
- Finalize alert thresholds with observability team (Diego) by T-24h.
- Lock the microwindow times and publish the release anchor doc to Confluence (Ava).
- Convert this sketch into the canonical runbook and attach automation snippets for throttle toggles (owner: Linh).

Notes to self: keep this canvas visible during the 48h preflight. Keep communication terse and timestamp actions in thread.
